chapter: Chicago, Lee Collins and the road
title: Sour mash dumped on Federal Street
summary: Racketeers dumped sour mash from their stills in the vacant lots where the boys played.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: And we'd play all up in Federal Street, and we'd play up in the lots up in there, and had this big pile of corn, about seven feet high. A big dump truck we saw come in the morning and dump this corn. We wondered what it was. It was sour mash that the racketeers were making at the still. Instead of going out on the dump and be exposed to it, they'd just find the first open dump, a lot with high weeds in it, and they saw it was abandoned houses and it was... You know, it was a slum. And they'd back this truck up in there and dump this; that dump truck would dump that corn, and you could smell it all over the neighborhood.
